The International Institute of St. Louis - an NGO that received over $33 million in government grants in 2024 - is offering assistance to Afghans, not Americans, not Caucasians, not Blacks. The program is only for Afghans.  
They will pay three months rent, three months of utilities, buy furniture, give them gift cards each month until they are approved to receive taxpayer funded welfare benefits including healthcare and food stamps. They are also getting ands-on help applying for SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, and refugee support services.  
They are also getting free bus tickets, sewing classes, entry onto volleyball teams, and an Afghan Entrepreneurship Grant - some of these migrants have already received $20,000 business grants.  
Its 2024 annual report shows that it received $33,280,786 in federal, state, and local grants. 
80.5% of their revenue comes from American tax dollars.  
The Institute’s plans are “to reverse decades of population decline, strengthen our workforce and grow our regional economies.”  
However, Former CEO Arrey Obenson said that St. Louis “cannot only be dependent on refugees that are sent to St. Louis by the federal government” as they are being supported by the government rather than contributing to the community.
